title: Adaptive prefix-pinning eviction protocol for KV cache to ensure atomicity and correctness under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Under continuous batching and high-concurrency workloads we see two interrelated failure modes: (1) GPU memory pressure triggers aggressive KV entry eviction that can race with active generation streams (leading to corrupted logits or silent token regressions), and (2) coarse LRU eviction does not respect semantic prefix affinity (many requests reuse the same conversation/key prefixes), causing frequent cache churn and higher token compute cost. Goals: design an eviction policy and protocol that (a) guarantees correctness/atomicity of KV reads during active generations, (b) provides prefix-aware retention to reduce thrashing, and (c) integrates with the runtime's batching scheduler and GPU memory allocator to maintain latency SLOs and bounded memory usage.
acceptance_criteria: No reproducible cases where an active generation reads partially-evicted KV resulting in corrupted token outputs (verified by integration fuzz tests),
End-to-end latency regressions <= 5% on p99 compared to baseline when feature is enabled under identical load,
Cache hit rate for prefix-heavy workloads improves by >= 20% in staged runs,
Evictions produce explicit telemetry (reason, prefix, epoch) and an alert fires if forced deallocations > 0.5% of in-flight generations,
Feature is gated behind runtime flag (disabled by default) and can be rolled back without model restarts.
implementation_notes:
High-level design:
1) Data structures:
   - Per-prefix metadata record: prefix_id -> {last_access_epoch (int), ttl_deadline (ms), refcount (atomic), pinned_until_epoch (int)}. Implemented as flat GPU-side arrays for hot prefixes + CPU fallback map for cold prefixes.
   - LRU slab allocator for KV values on GPU memory that supports O(1) eviction candidate selection but consults prefix metadata before reclaim.
2) Eviction policy (adaptive hybrid):
   - Active pinning: When a generation starts, the runtime increments refcount for all prefixes it will read/write; pinning prevents physical deallocation. Pin lifetime is tied to generation epoch id and is released on generation completion.
   - Prefix-aware priority: eviction score = base_LRU_score * decay_factor(prefix_hotness) * ttl_boost. Hot prefixes (recently accessed by many sessions or long-running chat threads) receive lower eviction score.
   - Soft TTL + hard TTL: soft TTL triggers background migration to host staging buffer; hard TTL marks for deallocation once refcount==0 and epoch < pinned_until_epoch.
   - Two-phase deallocation: mark -> grace epoch -> free. This prevents races with in-flight batched kernels that may still read KV pointers across micro-batches.
3) Concurrency controls and atomicity:
   - All GPU pointer swaps for KV updates are atomic 128-bit CAS operations where supported; otherwise use a double-buffer pattern (publish pointer after write complete).
   - Eviction sets a tombstone bit visible to readers; readers who observe tombstone either pin a temporary snapshot or trigger a synchronous fallback recompute.
4) Integration with continuous batching scheduler:
   - Scheduler consults prefix hotness and current pinned memory when forming batch windows. If pinned memory would cause SLO violation, scheduler prioritizes requests by prefix reuse to maximize cache benefit.
   - Eviction decisions feed back into autoscaler: sustained high eviction due to memory pressure triggers scale-up recommendations or activation of quantized model variants.
5) GPU memory optimizations:
   - Compact small KV entries into shared slab pools to reduce fragmentation.
   - Asynchronous GPU-to-CPU spill path: large/old prefixes spilled to host staging asynchronously; reads check host staging if GPU miss occurs.
6) Correctness invariants:
   - Readers observe either the complete pre-update KV snapshot or the complete post-update snapshot (no partial reads).
   - No generation sees a deallocated pointer: pinned entries are never reclaimed until all referencing epochs finish.
   - If an entry is unavailable, the runtime either recomputes deterministically or routes the request to a compatible fallback model variant.
Practical implementation notes:
- Start with CPU-only prototype to validate correctness semantics (refcounts, tombstone protocol) before GPU optimizations.
- Use lock-free atomic ops for refcount and epoch checks to avoid stalls in hot paths.
- Provide telemetry for: pin/unpin counts, tombstone hits, staged spills, reclaims, per-prefix hit rates.
- Add a self-check that verifies refcount sums equal expected in-flight references every 5s in debug builds.
testing_plan: Unit tests for per-prefix refcount lifecycle (increment, release, mark-for-evict semantics).
Deterministic integration tests: simulate continuous batching with interleaved prefix overlap; assert no partial KV reads and token-level determinism with and without eviction enabled.
Race fuzzing harness: coordinated threads that trigger simultaneous eviction and kernel read to reproduce edge races; run nightly with sanitizer builds.
Load test in staging: prefix-heavy workload (chat threads) and prefix-light workload (stateless prompts); collect p50/p95/p99 latency, hit-rate, and eviction telemetry.
Chaos test: random forced GC cycles and induced memory pressure; verify graceful degradation and no silent correctness failures.
Golden output regression: predefined prompt set must match baseline generation exactly when pins prevent eviction; any divergence must be triaged.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime flag 'kv.adaptive_pin_v1'. 2) Deploy CPU-only correctness prototype to canary (internal only) and run integration verification. 3) Enable GPU fast-path for 5% of traffic for non-critical tenants for 48h; monitor tombstone hits, eviction rate, p99 latency. 4) Expand to 25% with automatic fallback to disabled mode if deallocations > threshold or p99 regressions exceed 10%. 5) Full rollout for customers with SLAs only after 2 weeks of stable signals and RC sign-off. 6) Provide an opt-out flag for Dedicated/Private deployments during initial period.
